class_data.name: Spellcasting
class_data.notes:
You have learned to cast spells as a student of arcane magic.

Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice (Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended). Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Wizard cantrip of your choice. At Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional Wizard cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spellbook. Your studies culminated in the creation of your spellbook. It is a Tiny object (3 pounds, 100 pages) that can be read only by you or by someone casting Identify. You determine its appearance and materials.
The book contains the level 1+ Wizard spells you know. It begins with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice (Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended).
Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, you add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table.

Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Wizard spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose four spells from your spellbook. Each prepared spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
The number of prepared spells increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table; whenever that number increases, you choose additional spells from your spellbook to match the new total.
If another Wizard feature gives you spells that are always prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they count as Wizard spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of them with other spells from your spellbook.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook. The spells you gain when leveling reflect your ongoing research, but you can also add spells you find:
• Copying a Spell into the Book. When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it is of a level you can prepare and you have the time and resources. Copying takes 2 hours and 50 GP per spell level. Once copied, you can prepare the spell like any other in your book.
• Copying the Book. You can copy spells from your spellbook into another book. This is faster because you already know the spells: it takes 1 hour and 10 GP per spell level.
• Replacing a Lost Book. If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same process to transcribe the Wizard spells you currently have prepared into a new book. Filling out the remainder of the new spellbook requires you to find additional spells. Many wizards keep a backup spellbook for this reason.

class_data.name: Ritual Adept
class_data.notes: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if the spell has the Ritual tag and is in your spellbook. You need not have the spell prepared, but you must read from your spellbook when casting it as a Ritual.

class_data.name: Arcane Recovery
class_data.notes:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can recover expended spell slots with a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the recovered slots can be level 6 or higher.
For example, as a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots (one level 2 slot or two level 1 slots).
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

class_data.name: Scholar
class_data.notes: In addition to your magical studies, you specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You gain Expertise in the chosen skill.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes:
You choose a Wizard subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Wizard levels.

No Subclass Selected
Select a subclass to view its feature(s) here.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

class_data.name: Memorize Spell
class_data.notes: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with a different level 1+ Wizard spell from your spellbook.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes:
You gain a level 6 feature from your Wizard subclass.

No Subclass Selected
Select a subclass to view its feature(s) here.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

subclass_data.name: Bladesong
subclass_data.notes:
Bonus Action to activate. Requires no armor or shield.
Duration: 1 minute. Ends early if you are Incapacitated, wear armor/shield, or make a two-handed weapon attack.
Uses: Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). Regain all uses on Long Rest; regain 1 use when using Arcane Recovery.

Benefits while active:
• Agility: +INT modifier to AC (minimum +1), +10 ft. Speed, Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
• Bladework: Use Intelligence modifier for attack and damage rolls with proficient weapons.
• Focus: Add Intelligence modifier to Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.

subclass_data.name: Training in War and Song
subclass_data.notes:
Gain proficiency with all Melee Martial weapons that are not Two-Handed and not Heavy.
You can use a proficient Melee weapon as a Spellcasting Focus.
Gain proficiency in one skill: Acrobatics, Athletics, Performance, or Persuasion.

subclass_data.name: Extra Attack
subclass_data.notes:
When you take the Attack action, you may attack twice.
You may replace one of the attacks with a Wizard cantrip that has a casting time of 1 action.

class_data.name: Spellcasting
class_data.notes:
You draw on innate magic to cast Sorcerer spells.

Cantrips. You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice (Light, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp, and Sorcerous Burst are recommended). Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Sorcerer cantrip. At levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional Sorcerer cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spell Slots. The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Sorcerer spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose two level 1 spells (Burning Hands and Detect Magic are recommended). Your number of prepared spells increases as you gain levels, as shown in the class table, and the spells must be of levels for which you have spell slots.
If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that are always prepared, they don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they count as Sorcerer spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one prepared spell with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for Sorcerer spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Sorcerer spells.

class_data.name: Innate Sorcery
class_data.notes:
Your body holds simmering arcane power. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash this power for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits:
• Your Sorcerer spell save DC increases by 1.
• You have Advantage on attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

You can use this feature twice, regaining all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

class_data.name: Font of Magic
class_data.notes:
You have a wellspring of magic represented by Sorcery Points, which fuel certain magical effects.

You have 2 Sorcery Points at this level, and you gain more as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the class table. You can’t have more points than the amount listed for your level, and you regain all expended points when you finish a Long Rest.

You can use Sorcery Points for options like converting slots and Metamagic:
• Converting Spell Slots to Sorcery Points. You can expend a spell slot (no action required) to gain Sorcery Points equal to the slot’s level.
• Creating Spell Slots. As a Bonus Action, you can transform Sorcery Points into a spell slot. The Creating Spell Slots table (see creating_spell_slots_table) shows the Sorcery Point cost and minimum Sorcerer level for each slot level (up to level 5). Any slot created this way vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

class_data.name: Metamagic
class_data.notes:
Your inner magic lets you twist spells to suit your needs. You gain two Metamagic options of your choice from metamagic_options. You use these options to modify spells you cast by spending Sorcery Points.

You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless a Metamagic option specifically allows otherwise.

Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one Metamagic option you know with a different one. You gain two additional options at level 10 and two more at level 17.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes:
You choose a Sorcerer subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Sorcerer levels.

No Subclass Selected
Select a subclass to view its feature(s) here.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Sorcerer levels 8, 12, and 16.

subclass_data.name: Clockwork Spells
subclass_data.notes:
You always have the following spells prepared at the listed Sorcerer levels:

3rd: Aid, Alarm, Lesser Restoration, Protection from Evil and Good
5th: Dispel Magic, Protection from Energy
7th: Freedom of Movement, Summon Construct
9th: Greater Restoration, Wall of Force

Additionally, your spellcasting manifests visually or audibly. Choose or roll (1d6) on the Manifestations of Order table:
1. Spectral cogwheels hover behind you.
2. Clock hands spin in your eyes.
3. Your skin glows with a brassy sheen.
4. Floating equations and geometric shapes appear around you.
5. Your focus transforms into a Tiny clockwork device.
6. Ticking gears or clock chimes are heard by you and affected creatures.

subclass_data.name: Restore Balance
subclass_data.notes:
When a creature you can see within 60 feet would roll a d20 with Advantage or Disadvantage, you can use your Reaction to negate both, forcing a normal roll.

Uses: Charisma modifier (minimum 1). All uses restored after a Long Rest.

effects.name: Fey Ancestry
effects.notes: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Charmed condition.

effects.name: Fey Gift
effects.notes: You know the Friends cantrip. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace that cantrip with a different cantrip from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose the ability when you select this species).

effects.name: Lethargy Resilience
effects.notes: When you fail a saving throw to avoid or end the Unconscious condition, you can succeed instead. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish 1d4 Long Rests.

effects.name: Skill Versatility
effects.notes: You gain proficiency in one skill or with one tool of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace it with another skill or tool proficiency.

feats.notes: oncentration Breaker. When you damage a creature that is Concentrating, it has Disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain Concentration.Guarded Mind. If you fail an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw, you can cause yourself to succeed instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
feats.name: Mage Slayer

feats.notes: Your Hit Point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your character level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a character level thereafter, your Hit Point maximum increases by an additional 2 Hit Points.
feats.name: Tough

feats.notes: Energy Mastery. Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. Spells you cast ignore Resistance to damage of the chosen type. In addition, when you roll damage for a spell you cast that deals damage of that type, you can treat any 1 on a damage die as a 2.
feats.name: Elemental Adept

feats.notes: Bolstering Performance. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can give an inspiring performance: a speech, song, or dance. When you do so, choose up to six allies (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of yourself who witness the performance. The chosen creatures each gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your character level plus the modifier of the ability you increased with this feat.
feats.name: Inspiring Leader
